newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen steady after recent losses.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen steady after recent losses.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were called to open steady Thursday after sharp losses this week due to more generation units in West coming back to service and forecasts of cooler temperatures in the Southwest
"It's better bid out there," said a New York-based futures broker.

July California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were quoted at $17.25-17.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) compared with Wednesday's settlement at $17.14, while July Palo Verde (PV) were assessed at $27.25-27.50 against yesterday's close at $27.11.
July COB is at its lowest level in a month, while July PV is at its lowest since mid-May.

Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said the DC (direct current) segment of the Pacific Intertie, which carries hydropower from the Northwest to southern California, tripped offline Wednesday afternoon after a crane came in contact with the line.
BPA said it hoped to restore the DC portion of the intertie, rated at 3,100 megawatts (MW), by late yesterday or early today.
News of the line outage did bolster balance of June values at PV late Wednesday, market sources said.
Any recovery in the power complex could be capped by the return of two key nuclear power units in the West after recent outages and weakness in natural gas futures.

The 1,087 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear unit in central California was producing at 48 percent power early today, while the 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 unit near Phoenix, Arizona was operating at 80 percent.
The Southwest was forecast to see an unseasonally strong cold front through Sunday, with temperatures falling to around two to five degrees below normal.
Temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were forecast to average two to six degrees below normal over the same period.
NYMEX July Henry Hub natgas futures opened down 4.2 cents at $2.110 per million British thermal units.
